decision: Keep original main training and the planned E30 ordinary/fixed-CFG review. Do not start a larger batch-initialization trial or adopt a fitted batch-mean correction on these diagnostics. Continue the preplanned positive-CFG calibration and later independently validate the retained near-zero candidate.
interpretation: Generated batch-associated variation is larger, rather than simply underrepresented. Error batch effects do not improve held-out within-perturbation centered residual prediction across any of five perturbation folds at these sample sizes. The centered batch-composition vector is small relative to pseudobulk mean error. These results do not support a simple missing-batch-effect explanation.
limits: Effects are observational and noisy in both real and generated finite populations. The composition ratio is a descriptive squared norm, not a causal attribution or independent performance improvement. Most observed mean-error energy varies across perturbations, including Monte Carlo sampling effects; this does not establish one specific architecture or optimizer fault. No validation-fitted coefficients may be applied to test predictions.
